To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(a) there is a significant difference between the learning and teaching styles of engineering students and faculty; (b) this is not because engineering students are different from students in other fields; and (c) the differences are not due to age or gender.

(a) there are four dimensions on which students and teachers can be differentiated: (i) active/reflective (ii) sensing/intuitive (iii) visual/verbal and (iv) sequential/global, (b) these four dimensions are independent of one another, (c) these dimensions are not related to gender, and (d) the dimensions can be measured with a high degree of reliability and validity using the Index of Learning Style (ILS).
